newsitem.title: FINLAND: SMALL FINNISH ENGINEERING FIRMS CAN DO BETTER - KTM.
newsitem.headline: SMALL FINNISH ENGINEERING FIRMS CAN DO BETTER - KTM.

text.p: The competitiveness of small Finnish engineering companies is good relative to similar firms in Germany, France and the United Kingdom, but there is room for improvement, a government-sponsored report said on Monday.

"Based on a comparative study, it was possible to establish that the competitiveness of Finnish small- and medium-sized engineering companies is quite good compared to French, German and British (companies)," the ministry of trade and industry (KTM) said in a statement.
The Finnish firms studied were particularly competitive from the point of view of personnel costs, KTM said.
"The Finnish companies personnel costs were substantially lower than in the comparable French and German companies," it said.

In Finland, labour costs totalled 159,000 markka per year per employee, in France they were 213,000 markka and in Germany 254,000. In the United Kingdom, labour costs were the lowest at 123,000 markka per employee and year, KTM said.
Area where Finnish companies could improve their competitiveness were production efficiency and export marketing.

"A lot can still be done especially in the streamlining of production chains," KTM said, adding this showed it would be possible for Finnish engineering firms to further improve their competitiveness.
"There are also clear deficiencies in export marketing," it said.
